output.summary: The yield decline is real: the gauge R&R is stable and Halvard's reject rate rose (E4, E5). The new-operator cohort is ruled out, since their reject rate matches experienced operators and FPY fell before they ran alone (E14). The Corvane bar change, the deferred spindle service and the 12-hour shifts began within weeks of each other and are confounded. Hardness spread and spindle wear both fit the data, and scrap-tag times do not show when a part was machined, so fatigue is untested. Spindle runout and vibration are rising. Best next step is a staggered service plus Tamsworth trial lots with proper logging, and recovering the hour of machining and the Line 6 CMM data. Do not revert shifts as the root-cause fix, blame the new operators, or cut CMM inspection.
